title: Raising the Charge a Protection Plan Owes for Being Given Up
content:
The charge a Pass and Trip Protection plan owes for being given up stands on the plan's own protection account
as an amount the household owes. Raising it books that charge against the plan, and the amount still to be
collected on the plan rises by exactly that amount; the household sees the charge on the plan's protection
account whenever the account is read back to them.

**How the charge is raised.** The tool `raise_plan_giveup_charge_59dbe3e5` is unlocked and then called by the
desk. One call books a single plan fee entry of the amount given against the named plan, marked as the charge
for giving a plan up.

**What is passed to it.**

- `protection_plan_id` — the reference number of the protection plan the charge is raised on, as the
  protection plan lookup returns it.
- `fee_amount_usd` — the charge raised by this entry, in USD, given to 2 decimal places as a plain number such
  as 12.34 with no currency symbol and no thousands separator; it is booked to the cent exactly as passed.

**What comes back.** A single line of confirmation text naming the new protection account entry reference, the
protection plan it was booked on and the charge raised in USD to the cent. The line beginning with the word
Charged is the receipt that the entry was booked; any other wording means nothing was booked.
